clue.text: They upset some scholars about beginning of term

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters wrap round the extra letter
upset means knocked over, so the letters of some scholars are thrown into a new order
the beginning of a word is its opening letter, here taken from term

explanation.surface: Somebody upsets a group of scholars at the start of term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges SOME SCHOLARS into SCHOOLMASERS; 'about' wraps that round T, the 'beginning of' term. 'They' is the definition, pointing back to the wordplay: the teachers who might upset scholars.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue reads as a description of teachers, so the pronoun stands for the people who upset pupils at the start of a school term.

clue.text: Gets over life's burdens

definitions.meaning: to get over something, as a road or bridge, is to traverse it
troubles one must bear, as in 'we all have our cross to bear'

explanation.definitionFit: Traverses means getting over, and the plural noun means trials or burdens one has to carry through life.

clue.text: Ring-road, junction and by-pass

parts.note: a ring is round like the letter O
MI stands for the M1, Britain's main north-south motorway
a T-junction, where one road meets another at right angles

explanation.surface: A list of road features: ring-road, junction and bypass.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds; crosswords write it MI. 'by-pass' here is a verb, to skip.
explanation.definitionFit: To by-pass something is to skip or leave it out, a verb synonym.

clue.text: A record? Yes, of course

parts.note: a ship's record kept of the course it has sailed, with 'of course' read literally rather than as 'certainly'

explanation.definitionFit: A ship's or vehicle's journal records the route and events of a voyage, so it is a record of the course.

clue.text: Speech gets publicity coverage

parts.note: an ad is a piece of publicity
a dress covers the body

explanation.surface: A speech is reported widely in the press.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal talk given to an audience is a synonym for a speech.

clue.text: Fuel container in military vehicle

definitions.meaning: a vessel holding petrol in a car
an armoured fighting vehicle with tracks and a gun

explanation.definitionFit: The same word names both a petrol reservoir and an armoured battlefield vehicle.

clue.text: Catches, as one comes drunkenly home

definitions.meaning: an angler draws a hooked fish towards the bank
staggering through the door after too much drink

explanation.definitionFit: An angler winds in a hooked fish, and a drunk staggers in through the door; both are the phrase.

clue.text: Be in a fine state of suspense

definitions.text: Be in a fine state of suspense

parts.words: Be in a fine state of suspense
parts.note: being literally suspended from something very fine, a slender strand, while also being in a precarious situation

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to be in a precarious position, depending on one slender support.

clue.text: Sympathetic interpretation

definitions.meaning: kind and tolerant towards others' feelings
one's reading or grasp of a matter

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective for being tolerant and kind and a noun for comprehension or reading of something.

clue.text: Loving having a party telephone

parts.note: a do is an informal party
to ring someone is to telephone them

explanation.surface: Someone affectionate has a party line on the phone.
explanation.definitionFit: Doting and fond, a direct synonym for loving.

clue.text: Prison for debt-collector who has gone astray

parts.note: a dun is one who demands payment of debts

indicators.note: astray means wandering off course, so the letters of gone are jumbled

explanation.surface: A debt-collector who has gone off the rails ends up in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'astray' is the anagram signal. A dun is an old word for someone who pesters debtors for payment.
explanation.definitionFit: An underground cell in a castle is a kind of prison.

clue.text: The point in running is to win

indicators.note: in signals that the answer sits inside the following words

explanation.surface: A sporting maxim: the point of racing is to win.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'runninG IS To'; 'win' just completes the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The essential meaning or main thrust of something is its point.

clue.text: Sailing-centre we found in Greek island

indicators.note: found in means placed inside, so we goes within the island's name

parts.note: Cos (or Kos) is a Greek island in the Dodecanese

explanation.surface: Somebody says a sailing centre was discovered on a Greek island.
explanation.walkthrough: COWES is a town on the Isle of Wight, home of Cowes Week, a famous yachting regatta.
explanation.definitionFit: A town famous for its annual yachting regatta is a sailing centre.

clue.text: Is half left in the water

indicators.note: half of a four-letter word is its first two letters, here from left

explanation.surface: Is half of something left floating in the water?
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' takes LE from left. The definition is descriptive: land in the water.
explanation.definitionFit: An island is a piece of land surrounded by water, so it is found in the water.

clue.text: Project that is captivating politician supported by Left

indicators.note: in a down answer a piece supported by another sits above it
captivating means holding captive, so the letters for 'that is' enclose the politician

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, that is
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A project championed by a politician backed by the Left.
explanation.definitionFit: To project something is to propel or thrust it forward, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Points gained from scratch

definitions.meaning: the tally of points in a game
to scratch a line or mark into a surface

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a game's tally and to cut a line into a surface.

clue.text: Feature film about the Middle East?

definitions.text: Feature film about the Middle East?

parts.words: Feature film about the Middle East?
parts.note: not a movie but a thin covering (film) over the face (features) worn in the Middle East

explanation.definitionFit: A veil worn over the face by some Muslim women is a covering film over the features.

clue.text: Extra helpings or extras helping

definitions.meaning: further servings of food after the first
assistants to a duellist or boxer

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both second servings at a meal and attendants who assist duellists or boxers.

clue.text: They may commemorate different battles

indicators.note: different means changed, so the letters of battles are put in another order

explanation.definitionFit: Stone plaques bearing inscriptions are used to commemorate people and events.

clue.text: It helps a tramp to settle down

definitions.text: It helps a tramp to settle down

parts.words: It helps a tramp to settle down
parts.note: a tramp is a cargo steamer without a fixed route; heavy material in its hold keeps it low and steady, not a vagrant settling

explanation.definitionFit: Heavy material carried low in a ship's hold gives it stability in the water.

clue.text: Drink with more merry C-in-C

parts.note: to sup is to drink

indicators.note: merry means tipsy, so the letters of more are jumbled

explanation.surface: A commander-in-chief has a drink and gets merrier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'merry' is the anagram signal, reading as tipsy in the surface. C-in-C is commander-in-chief.
explanation.definitionFit: A supreme leader or overall boss is like a commander-in-chief.

clue.text: She made her name in drama

indicators.note: made means constructed, so the letters of 'in drama' are assembled anew

explanation.surface: An actress made her name on the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' rearranges IN DRAMA. Miranda is also the heroine of Shakespeare's The Tempest, so she has her name in drama.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's name stands for the pronoun she.

clue.text: Pitch of the road

parts.note: pitch read as tar, the black surface material laid on highways, not slope

explanation.definitionFit: A road surface of broken stone bound with tar is the material of a road.

clue.text: Hastened up with speed to tell the tale

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: ran means hastened
rate means speed

explanation.surface: Someone hurried up quickly to tell a story.
explanation.definitionFit: To recount a story is to tell the tale.

clue.text: Register for a continental breakfast?

definitions.meaning: a bread ... is part of a light European breakfast

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a register of names and a small bread loaf served at breakfast.

clue.text: A step made quickly

parts.note: a pace is a step

explanation.definitionFit: Apace is an old-fashioned word meaning swiftly.

clue.text: First part of rust in rotten nail

indicators.note: in means the letter goes inside the word for rotten

parts.note: bad means rotten

indicators.note: the first part of a word is its opening letter, from rust

explanation.definitionFit: A brad is a thin, small-headed nail.

clue.text: Young pig is a good investment

definitions.meaning: a young female pig, a sow that has not yet farrowed
a ...-edged security, a safe government stock

explanation.definitionFit: The word is a young sow and also a safe government bond.

clue.text: Divinity is a course at Oxford

definitions.meaning: the name of the Thames as it flows through Oxford, course meaning watercourse

explanation.definitionFit: The Egyptian mother goddess is a divinity, and the Thames at Oxford goes by the same name.

clue.text: It may make a man keen on money, and a woman on food

definitions.text: It may make a man keen on money

indicators.note: on means placed next to, the woman's name set before the food

parts.note: Ava is a woman's name
rice is a food

explanation.surface: Greed makes a man love money, as a woman might love food.
explanation.definitionFit: Greed for wealth is what makes a person keen on money.

clue.text: Dad is wrong in showing contempt

indicators.note: wrong means not right, so the letters of 'Dad is' are put out of order

explanation.surface: Dad is mistaken in showing scorn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges DAD IS into DISDA, followed by IN as written.
explanation.definitionFit: Scorn or lack of respect is a synonym for contempt.

clue.text: Changing to steam trains? He should know

indicators.note: changing means altering, so the letters of 'to steam trains' are rearranged

explanation.surface: A passenger asks about changing to steam trains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changing' rearranges TO STEAM TRAINS. The definition is cryptic: the person in charge of a railway station would know.
explanation.definitionFit: The railway official running a station is the one who would know about trains.
